title: Streamed HTML that the canvas draws as it arrives
shows: Markup streamed into a drawable element with streamAppendHTML(), from the Prompt API or from a fetch. The paint event's changedElements names each new block, and the canvas draws new blocks through an effect (noise that resolves into the text, a scan line, ink that spreads) while older blocks are already plain and selectable.
build: One drawable article element. A WritableStream from streamAppendHTML() takes chunks from LanguageModel.promptStreaming() where the model is on the device, and from a Workers AI endpoint otherwise. A per-block age map drives one uniform per block. A second mode uses out-of-order streaming: the server sends a page skeleton, then fills sections in a different order, and each section arrives with its own effect.
measured: streamAppendHTML() raised one paint event per chunk with no requestPaint() in Chromium 157.
uncertain: Whether changedElements lists the new block or only the container. Whether the Prompt API model is downloadable on the test phone (the test browser reports downloadable for LanguageModel and Summarizer but cannot fetch a model). Streaming methods are missing in Chromium 153, so the page needs a fallback that appends with setHTML().
needs: A device with the on-device model for the Prompt API path. The fetch path runs anywhere.

title: A CSS-only carousel drawn as a cover flow
shows: A scroller with scroll snap, ::scroll-marker and ::scroll-button(), written with no script, drawn by a canvas as a ring of tilted cards. The native markers and buttons are drawn where the scene wants them and still scroll the real list. Keyboard, touch fling and the accessibility tree are the scroller's own.
build: Each slide is a drawable child, drawn with a perspective transform taken from its offset to the scroll position. sibling-index() gives each slide its slot on the ring. A scroll-state(snapped) query sets a custom property on the snapped slide, which the canvas reads as the focus uniform. A second layout draws multicol ::column fragments as book pages with a page-turn shader.
measured: Marker and button pseudo-elements are in the element picture, and a real click on a drawn marker scrolled the list (Chromium 153 and 157). A scroll-state(stuck) query restyled a drawn element and raised a paint event by itself.
uncertain: Whether markers can be drawn apart from their scroller: they are part of the scroller's picture, so moving them means drawing the scroller twice with different clips. Touch fling on a scroller whose slides are drawn away from their layout boxes.

title: Native popovers, hints and commands on warped surfaces
shows: Controls drawn on a 3D panel, a cloth or under a lens that open real top-layer UI: a popover=hint from interestfor, a popover or dialog from commandfor, a customisable select. The popover is positioned with CSS anchor positioning and stays attached to the place where its control is drawn.
build: Popovers live outside the canvas, because a popover inside a drawn element is not in its picture. Each one uses position-anchor on the drawn control. The page records, for every surface type on the site (2D transform, perspective quad, deforming mesh, lens), whether the anchored popover follows. anchored(fallback) queries flip the popover's arrow when the surface turns away.
measured: In Chromium 157 an element anchored to a canvas child follows the drawn position (moved by 100,50 when the child was drawn at 100,50), and hovering a drawn interestfor button opened its hint. Both failed in Chromium 153, where the anchor stays at the layout box. commandfor on a drawn button opened a popover in both.
uncertain: What the anchor rectangle is under a perspective transform set with updateElementGeometry(): the bounding box of the quad, or nothing. Whether Chrome 159 on the phone behaves like 157.

title: HDR interface: elements brighter than white
shows: Ordinary DOM drawn into a float16 canvas, with chosen pixels raised above standard white on an HDR screen: a primary button that emits light, a focus ring that blooms, a notification badge at 4 times white. dynamic-range-limit keeps body text at standard brightness.
build: A 2D context with colorType 'float16', colorSpace 'display-p3' and, in Chrome 160, toneMapping 'extended'. Draw the element, then composite it again with 'lighter' through a mask made from a CSS custom property (--glow). A WebGPU path uses an rgba16float canvas with toneMapping extended and a bloom pass. A slider sets the headroom. A dynamic-range media query shows a notice on a standard screen.
measured: In a float16 Display P3 canvas, color(display-p3 1 0 0) on a drawn element read back as 1, 0, 0 and color(srgb-linear 4 4 4) read back as 1.82, so values above 1.0 survive drawElementImage() (Chromium 153 and 157).
uncertain: Whether values above 1.0 reach the screen from a 2D canvas before Chrome 160. Whether texElementSubImage2D() and drawElementImageToTexture() keep them in a 16-bit float texture. Why 4.0 read back as 1.82 (a tone curve or a limit).
needs: An HDR screen. Most recent Android phones have one.

title: Shader uniforms written in CSS only
shows: The fx attribute with no script on the page author's side: uniforms come from typed attr(), @function presets, if() and style range queries, sibling-index() for stagger, random() for per-element seeds, progress() for mapping sizes and scroll positions to 0 to 1.
build: Extend shader-fx.js to enumerate --fx-* custom properties with getComputedStyle() and bind each to the uniform of the same name. Register the effect name as a string property so it cascades. Load shader files with import ... with { type: 'text' }. A gallery of twelve cards, each a CSS rule and nothing else.
measured: random() keeps one value per element across paints in Chromium 157, so a seed does not flicker.
uncertain: Cost of enumerating computed style each frame. random() and text import are missing in Chromium 153, so each feature needs an @supports fallback.

title: Scroll-linked shaders with no scroll listener
shows: Scroll-driven and scroll-triggered CSS animations that animate registered custom properties, which a canvas reads as uniforms. A sticky header that is drawn through a blur once scroll-state(stuck) matches. Sections that burn in when a timeline trigger fires. A pull-to-reveal drawer on the overscroll area that stretches with the pull.
build: A long article where each section is a drawable child of one tall canvas, or each section is its own canvas-slot. animation-timeline: view() drives --fx-progress. scroll-state queries set flags. Wheel momentum and scroll promises time the effects.
measured: A scroll-driven animation inside a drawn element repaints by itself: after scrolling, the paint event fired with no requestPaint() and both the colour animation and the transform animation were at their end state (Chromium 153 and 157).
uncertain: Whether a compositor-driven scroll animation raises a paint event every frame on a real GPU, or only when the main thread catches up. This decides whether the effect lags the scroll on a phone.

title: CSS shapes lit as solid objects
shows: Buttons and cards with corner-shape, border-shape, shape() and rounded polygon() outlines, drawn through a shader that uses the element's alpha as a height field: bevels catch light, a squircle key presses down, a notched ticket casts a shadow with the right outline.
build: Blur the alpha channel of the element texture to get a distance estimate, take its gradient as a normal, light it. background-clip: border-area and gap decorations give rim and groove detail from CSS. shape-outside: shape() wraps page text around the same outline.
measured: corner-shape: bevel, border-shape: circle(), clip-path: shape() and gap decorations are all applied in the element picture (Chromium 153 and 157).
uncertain: Quality of normals from blurred alpha at small radii. Whether hit testing follows border-shape or the border box.

title: Text measured by CSS for textures, signs and particles
shows: Labels for 3D objects whose texture is exactly the ink: text-box-trim removes the space above and below, text-fit fills the width, sideways writing modes give vertical labels. Glyph particles for the text a user types into an input, using OpaqueRange rects. Variable font axes animated in CSS on a sign in a scene.
build: A scene with signs, a spine label and a ticker. Each label is a drawable element sized by CSS only. For inputs, input.createValueRange() gives per-character rects that feed the existing glyph field. In Chrome 160, compare with TextMetrics.getSelectionRects().
measured: text-fit scaled a 10px word to 275 of 280 px in the picture. OpaqueRange rects for text in a drawn input moved by 80,60 when the input was drawn at 80,60 (Chromium 157; in 153 they did not move).
uncertain: Whether OpaqueRange rects are per glyph cluster or per code unit for complex scripts.

title: Carets, highlights and editing drawn through shaders
shows: A text editor on a 3D monitor with a block caret from CSS, a shader that smears the caret between positions, proofreader corrections as animated custom highlights, and find-in-page matches that pulse. This strand shares ground with the text selection effects thread.
build: caret-animation: manual stops the blink; the shader finds the caret by colour key and draws motion from the last two positions. Custom highlights use one keyed colour through ::highlight(*). highlightsFromPoint() makes highlighted words clickable where they are drawn. A second editor uses EditContext with the canvas drawing all text.
measured: The block caret is in the picture (215 px against 24 px for a bar). Custom highlights are in the picture. highlightsFromPoint() returns the highlight at the drawn position in Chromium 157 and nothing in 153.
uncertain: Whether the find-in-page highlight is painted into the picture (needs a person with the find bar open). Whether spelling markers are painted.

title: What a canvas may not see or wrap
shows: A measurement page for content the browser protects: permission elements (geolocation, camera, microphone, usermedia, install), :visited links, system colours, spelling markers, autofill previews, cross-origin iframes. For each one: is it drawn, can script read it, does it still work when drawn away from its box or through a shader.
build: One row per case with a live fixture and a recorded result, in the style of the element catalogue. A person completes the rows that need a real click or a real permission prompt.
measured: Capability elements are drawn as canvas children, and <geolocation> reports isValid false with the reason intersection_occluded_or_distorted. A canvas gets links drawn as unvisited while the screen shows the :visited colour (Chromium 153). AccentColor and Highlight read back as fixed default colours in the test browser.
uncertain: Whether a capability element becomes valid when it is drawn exactly over its layout box with no transform. What AccentColor reads back as inside an installed app.
needs: A person for the permission prompts.

title: Tilt the phone to light a live card
shows: A payment card, a ticket and a badge that are live DOM, drawn through foil, hologram and lenticular shaders whose light direction comes from the phone's orientation. Buttons on the card still work.
build: A button calls DeviceOrientationEvent.requestPermission(). Orientation sets two uniforms. With no sensor, the pointer position stands in. Haptic ticks mark the angle at which a lenticular image flips, where the haptics API exists.
uncertain: Sensor rate and latency on the phone. Web haptics is in developer trial from Chrome 156 and is missing from the test browser.

title: A lens that translates, simplifies or summarises what is under it
shows: Move a lens over a page and read the text under it in another language, in simpler words, or as a summary. On the board, a tile that is too small to read is replaced by a summary drawn at a readable size.
build: A hidden twin of the subtree is a second drawable child. Its text nodes are translated with Translator (source language from LanguageDetector) or rewritten with Rewriter. The lens draws the twin, clipped to the lens circle, at the same position as the original. Results are cached per text node.
measured: In the test browser Translator.availability() returned downloadable in Chromium 153; LanguageModel and Summarizer returned downloadable in 157. No model can be downloaded there.
uncertain: Line breaks differ between languages, so the twin's layout drifts from the original; the lens may need to align per block. Model availability and speed on a phone.
needs: A device with the built-in AI models.

title: An agent operating a canvas UI, drawn as it happens
shows: A form in a 3D scene that exposes WebMCP tools. When an agent calls a tool, the canvas draws the action on the live DOM: a marker travels to the field, the value types in, the panel turns to face the camera. A second mode gives the Prompt API a picture of the drawn UI and asks it what it sees.
build: navigator.modelContext tools wrap the form's actions. Each tool call returns after its animation. ariaNotify() announces the same steps. The picture for the multimodal prompt comes from canvas.toBlob(), after the shader.
measured: navigator.modelContext is missing from both test browsers.
uncertain: The WebMCP origin trial's API shape in Chrome 159. Whether the on-device model takes image input on a phone.
needs: The WebMCP origin trial or flag, and the on-device model.

title: Speak a label to press what the canvas draws
shows: On-device speech recognition biased to the labels of the controls drawn this frame. Saying a label presses the control, wherever the shader has put it. A transcript is drawn as DOM, with each word highlighted at its spoken time.
build: Collect accessible names of visible controls into SpeechRecognition phrases. Match results to controls and call click(). Result timestamps (Chrome 159) drive custom highlights on the transcript.
uncertain: On-device recognition availability on Android. Timestamps need Chrome 159.
needs: A microphone and a device with the on-device recognition model.

title: Page navigations drawn by a shader that starts at the clicked link
shows: A small multi-view site where every navigation is intercepted. The old view is kept as an ElementImage, the new view loads during the precommit phase, and a shader runs between the two pictures, starting from the box of the link that was clicked. Both views are live during the transition.
build: navigation.addEventListener('navigate') with a precommitHandler. NavigateEvent.sourceElement gives the origin point. Compare with element-scoped view transitions on the view transitions page.
uncertain: Whether an ElementImage of the old view stays drawable after its element is removed. Soft navigation and LCP accounting for a canvas-drawn view.

title: Controller, keyboard and haptic navigation of drawn UI
shows: A toolbar on a curved panel with focusgroup arrow keys. A gamepad moves focus between drawn controls with event-driven input and confirms with the standard button type. Each focus move plays a haptic tick. reading-flow states the drawn order where it differs from DOM order.
build: focusgroup attributes on the DOM. Gamepad events map to focus() calls with focusVisible. A table records, per surface, whether focus rings and arrow keys behave.
measured: focusgroup ArrowRight moved focus between buttons drawn in a canvas (Chromium 153 and 157).
uncertain: The gamepad event API is an origin trial from Chrome 149. Haptics is in developer trial.
needs: A gamepad for the controller part.

title: Latency from DOM change to canvas pixels, and a device tier
shows: New rows for the performance wall: time from a DOM change to presentation for plain DOM against a canvas-drawn element, style and layout time per frame from Long Animation Frames, and effect quality chosen from the CPU Performance API before the first frame.
build: elementtiming attributes on canvas children, a PerformanceObserver for element and long-animation-frame entries, navigator.cpuPerformance for the tier.
measured: Element Timing entries with presentationTime are reported for text and an image inside a drawable canvas (Chromium 153 and 157).
uncertain: Whether presentationTime is the frame in which the element was painted or the frame in which the canvas showed it.

title: New routes for the transport lab and the remote component
shows: WebTransport datagrams as a pixel route. Element Capture against canvas.captureStream(). WebRTC with its own adaptation turned off so text stays sharp. Input events handled in a worker. SharedArrayBuffer routes under Document-Isolation-Policy. What happens to each route when Android freezes the source tab after one minute.
build: Add routes to the lab's table. A Worker endpoint echoes WebTransport datagrams. The cross-tab page states the freeze rules it measured.
uncertain: WebTransport needs an HTTP/3 endpoint; Cloudflare Workers support has to be checked. Element Capture needs a tab-capture prompt, which headless cannot answer.
needs: The phone for SharedWorker on Android and the freeze timing.

title: Media state in CSS for canvas-drawn players
shows: Custom video controls drawn by the canvas that restyle from :playing, :paused, :buffering and :muted with no event listeners. A visualiser delayed by the measured output latency. Rows for lazy-loaded video and the not-rendered iframe policy.
build: Additions to the video and audio pages.
uncertain: Media pseudo-classes ship in Chrome 158; the test browser is 157.

title: Capture additions: clipboard, print margins, files
shows: Copy an element as a picture and as HTML in one clipboard item. Page headers and numbers on a printed capture with @page margin boxes. Save to a folder on Android. A board that watches a folder of HTML files and redraws a tile when its file changes.
build: Additions to element-capture.js and the board.
uncertain: FileSystemObserver on Android.

title: Packaging the custom elements with newer DOM features
shows: canvas-slot, dom-portal and dom-lens defined in a scoped registry, with manual slot assignment from declarative shadow DOM, Reference Target for labels, snapshots closed with using, and paint events as an Observable.
build: A branch of the libraries with feature checks, and a page that lists which feature removed which line of code.
uncertain: Whether a scoped registry changes how slotted children are found by the canvas.

title: Iframes as tiles: sizing, prerender and limits
shows: Board tiles that take their height from the embedded document, cross-origin tiles that are prerendered, a focus policy on embedded content, and a record of what a shader may do to a cross-origin iframe.
build: Additions to the board and to slot-view.
uncertain: Cross-origin iframe prerendering ships in Chrome 159 and needs a response header from the embedded origin.

title: DOM drawn across a fold
shows: One canvas across both halves of a foldable. In the half-folded posture the upper half shows content and the lower half shows controls, and the hinge is drawn as a crease that the DOM bends over.
build: navigator.devicePosture and visualViewport.segments choose the layout. DevTools has a foldable emulation for a first pass.
uncertain: Segment geometry on real devices.
needs: A foldable device, or DevTools emulation.

title: HTML panels in a real room
shows: HTML panels pressed with fingertips, attached to detected walls and tables, hidden behind real objects with depth sensing, and composited as WebXR quad layers for sharp text.
build: Extensions to html3d.js and the XR page: a hand pointer beside the controller ray, plane anchors, a depth test in the panel shader, a layer path that uploads elements with texElementSubImage2D().
uncertain: The cloud browser has no immersive session, so all of it is unverified. Whether texElementSubImage2D() can target a layer's texture.
needs: A headset, or an Android phone with ARCore for planes and depth.

title: Live DOM on physical devices
shows: Each key of a Stream Deck shows a live HTML button and pressing the key clicks it. A receipt printer prints a drawn element from the phone. An LED matrix shows a ticker that is a DOM marquee.
build: Draw each element into a small canvas, read the pixels, convert (JPEG per key for HID, 1-bit dither for ESC/POS, RGB565 for a matrix) and send. A simulated device panel on the page shows the same bytes for people with no hardware.
uncertain: Device protocols differ per model. WebHID is listed as shipping in Chrome 158 and Web Serial on Android in 148.
needs: A Stream Deck, a serial or Bluetooth printer, or an LED matrix.

title: WebGPU features for element textures
shows: Compatibility mode as a tier in the backend picker. Subpixel text on 3D surfaces with dual source blending. Per-shard effects from primitive_index. Per-element uniforms with immediates. Float accumulation targets for trails. Alpha-as-mask with texture swizzle.
build: Changes in backend.js and gpu-util.js with a row per feature in the WebGPU findings.
measured: The software adapter in Chromium 153 reports a compatibility adapter and the features float32-blendable, texture-component-swizzle, subgroups and clip-distances. Chromium 157 headless has no adapter.
uncertain: A render pass loses the device in the cloud browser, so every item needs a real GPU.
needs: A real GPU: the phone or a desktop.

title: An installed app whose window frame is a canvas
shows: The title bar, the window buttons and the content of an installed app, all drawn by one canvas with a shader over them. Drag regions come from window-drag on drawable children. On ChromeOS, an Isolated Web App sets its window shape from the outline of an element.
build: A manifest with window-controls-overlay, the windowing controls API for the buttons, and an install button from navigator.install().
uncertain: Whether window-drag applies to an element at its drawn position or at its layout box. Window Shape is limited to allowlisted Isolated Web Apps.
needs: A desktop install. ChromeOS for the window shape.

title: WebAssembly toolkits and models over live elements
shows: A Wasm UI toolkit whose render loop waits for the paint event through JSPI. A WebNN model that runs on the texture of a live element as a shader stage.
build: Follow-ups to the native UI page.
measured: navigator.ml is missing from both test browsers.
uncertain: WebNN is an origin trial from Chrome 147.
needs: The WebNN origin trial and a GPU.

title: Partial updates and moved elements drawn by a canvas
shows: Tiles in a canvas hold named ranges written as processing instructions. A stream of <template for> elements fills the ranges out of order, adds a new drawable tile at a marker, and moveBefore() reorders the tiles while an input keeps its focus. The canvas shows which tile a patch is landing in and flies each tile from its old place to its new one.
build: Each tile is a drawable element with its own texture. Patches are written with streamAppendHTMLUnsafe() in small chunks. A MutationObserver records which tile changed; the paint event's changedElements says which tiles to upload again. A move records the drawn place of every tile, calls moveBefore(), and interpolates each quad to the tile's new layout box.
measured: In Chromium 157 a streamed template patched a range that was already in a canvas child, one paint event was raised per chunk, changedElements named only the patched tile, a drawable element added by a patch was drawn at the next paint, and moveBefore() kept focus, selection and animation time. The sanitising stream methods dropped the patch.
uncertain: Whether Chrome 159 on the phone has <template for> and the Unsafe streaming methods. Chromium 153 has neither.
needs: Nothing beyond a browser with the features.
